meta.drug: pemafibrate (K-877; Parmodia in Japan), 0.2 mg twice daily
meta.mechanism: Selective peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha modulator (SPPARM-alpha); raises lipoprotein lipase activity, lowers apoC-III, lowers triglycerides and triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remnants by ~26% vs placebo but raises LDL-C (~12%) and apoB (~5%) through conversion of remnants to LDL
meta.indication: reduction of cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes with mild-to-moderate hypertriglyceridemia (TG 200-499 mg/dL) and low HDL-C (<=40 mg/dL) on guideline-directed statin therapy (primary and secondary prevention)

consensus_explanation.summary: Pemafibrate did what it was designed to do on its intended biomarker (triglycerides, VLDL-C, remnant cholesterol and apoC-III all about 26% lower than placebo), yet events were unchanged (HR 1.03, 0.91-1.15). The explanation accepted by the trial authors, the NEJM editorialist (Virani) and the Copenhagen group (Doi, Langsted, Nordestgaard) is that triglyceride level per se is not the causal quantity. What matters is the number of atherogenic apoB-containing particles, and pemafibrate converted triglyceride-rich remnants into LDL instead of clearing them: LDL-C rose about 12%, apoB rose 4.8% and non-HDL-C did not change. Mendelian randomization published before the readout (Ference 2019: TG-lowering LPL variants protect only in proportion to apoB lowering) predicts no benefit when apoB does not fall, and Doi et al. showed that the absolute changes in remnant cholesterol, LDL-C and apoB reproduce the observed HR (estimated 1.05 vs observed 1.03). As a secondary reason, the TG lowering (26%) was smaller than in the earlier Japanese trials (about 43-45%) on an intensive statin background with LDL-C already about 78 mg/dL; sponsor-affiliated authors (Fruchart et al.) say the reasons are uncertain and point to this attenuation and the low LDL-C. The trial itself was large, well run and stopped for futility. Its excess of renal events and venous thromboembolism is a separate safety finding, not the cause of the null result.

pre_readout.note: Readout = Kowa press release 2022-04-08 (topline only: DSMB futility, no numbers). Numeric results first at AHA 2022 / NEJM online 2022-11-05. Sources with pub_date before 2022-04-08 counted as available.
available_before_readout: Registry record (S3, first posted 2017-03-07): eligibility (TG 200-499, HDL-C <=40, T2D), primary outcome (current registry text shows the amended 4-component endpoint; original-version text not verified).
Design paper (S4, 2018-09-29): ~10,000 patients, 1092 primary events, >=90% power for 18% RRR, expected follow-up 3.75 y, original primary end point.
Japanese phase 2 (S12, 2016-02-26): TG -42.7% from baseline at 0.2 mg BID over 12 weeks; apoB reported as improved.
Japanese T2D phase 3 lipid trial (S13, 2018-01-03): TG ~45% lower vs placebo; LDL-C not considerably altered; apoB100 and non-HDL-C decreased.
APOC3 loss-of-function genetics (S10, S11, 2014-06-18): lower TG and CHD risk.
Ference 2019 LPL vs LDLR Mendelian randomization (S9, 2019-01-29): benefit of TG lowering proportional to apoB change.
PPARA drug-target MR (S14, 2021-10-21): no TG-based genetic validation of PPARA.
only_after_readout: All PROMINENT lipid effects (TG -26.2%, LDL-C +12.3%, apoB +4.8%, non-HDL-C -0.2%) and outcome HR 1.03 (0.91-1.15), 572 vs 560 events (S1, 2022-11-05).
Mid-trial endpoint change (March 2020) and event target increase 1092 -> 1304 described in S1 (whether the registry showed it before 2022-04-08 was not verified).

Absolute LDL-C (+0.26 mmol/L) and apoB (+5 mg/dL) changes come from a secondary analysis abstract (Doi 2024, S7), not from the NEJM paper.
Non-HDL-C absolute change is derived (-0.2% x 128 mg/dL = -0.007 mmol/L); Doi 2024 instead reports +3 mg/dL 'total atherogenic cholesterol' (remnant + LDL-C), a different construct.

Primary end point and event target were changed in March 2020 (blinded); whether the registry showed the amended endpoint before the 2022-04-08 readout was not verified (registry history not checked).
Virani NEJM editorial (S5) not read; its view is taken from MDedge quotes (S6).
Alpha sidedness not stated explicitly ('overall type 1 error at the 5% significance level'); assumed two-sided.
PPARA human genetics: the only drug-target MR found instruments PPARA via LDL-C; no genetic validation of PPARA-mediated TG lowering for CHD was found -> target_genetics 'uncertain'.
Registry results (final database, 2025) give 590 vs 570 events, HR 1.03 (0.92-1.16), vs NEJM 572 vs 560, HR 1.03 (0.91-1.15); NEJM values used.
